clue.text: Cornered and grabbed broken leg

indicators.note: grabbed means the word and holds the other letters within it

parts.note: taken as written here as fodder, not a link

indicators.note: broken says the letters of leg are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone was caught in a corner and seized with a fractured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a mere link between definition and wordplay, but here it is the container that does the grabbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something angled has been driven into a corner, as a cornered animal or a ball angled into a pocket.

clue.text: Endorse if a try is converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Approving a rugby try that is then converted for extra points.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a try is 'converted' by kicking the follow-up goal; here 'is converted' rearranges IFATRY.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify an agreement is to give it formal approval, a synonym.

clue.text: Trendy company's failing

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A fashionable business is going under.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak in health, the adjective sense of failing as in failing eyesight.

clue.text: Crawler longing to hold son and mother

indicators.note: to hold means the longing word wraps round the family letters

parts.note: a yen is a longing
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A sycophant yearning to embrace their son and mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawler is a toady who agrees with everything the boss says, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Rehashed tune and it remains pure

indicators.note: rehashed means reworked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recycled melody somehow stays unspoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rehashed' rearranges TUNE, AND and IT; 'remains' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Untainted means free from contamination, a synonym of pure.

clue.text: A change of oil to put in jet's mechanical flyer

indicators.note: a change of these words means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Swapping the oil in a jet engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges OILTOPUT after the A; 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic pilot is the device that flies an aircraft without a human hand on the controls.

clue.text: Free to be in a London shop?

definitions.text: to be in a London shop?
definitions.meaning: Liberty is a famous department store on Regent Street, London, so being there is being at it

explanation.surface: Being free to visit a shop in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberty is a well-known London department store; the question mark flags the punning second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at liberty is unconfined, able to go where they please.

clue.text: Centres charged for clue in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means jumbled up, so the letters of clue and in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is billed for a messy crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' belongs with the definition: atomic cores carry a positive charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic nuclei are the positively charged cores of atoms, the plural of a core.

clue.text: How a game of chess might end for a prisoner

definitions.text: How a game of chess might end
definitions.meaning: a chess game can finish '...', with checkmate

explanation.definitionFit: A game finishing in checkmate ends 'in mate', and a convict is a jail occupant.

clue.text: Pelt some aloof urbanites

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Throwing things at a few stand-offish city dwellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is an animal's hairy coat, a synonym.

clue.text: Time of the week when dynamo breaks down

indicators.note: breaks down means falls apart, so the letters of dynamo are reassembled

explanation.surface: The day each week when the generator fails.
explanation.definitionFit: The first working day is a fixed point in the seven-day cycle.

clue.text: Article you and I dread

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
we is the pronoun for you and I together

explanation.surface: A piece of writing the two of us are afraid of.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential fear, so it shares the sense of dread.

clue.text: Some confirm ant isn't predatory insect

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Checking that a certain ant isn't the hunting bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying variety is a famous carnivorous insect that ambushes its prey.

clue.text: Excellent student to be indisposed

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I standing for the one
L is a learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A top pupil being under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI in crosswords; L is the learner plate on a British student driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to be unwell, a synonym of being indisposed.

clue.text: Bird having a quick swim?

definitions.meaning: a small bird that bobs in streams
someone taking a dip, a brief swim, is jocularly one who dips

explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a stream-dwelling songbird, and a person taking a dip is jokingly one too.

clue.text: Some inspecting preserve gel

indicators.note: some says only part of the next word is wanted, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Examining a jar of jam set.
explanation.definitionFit: This fruit substance is the setting agent that makes jam and jelly firm.

clue.text: Prize when part of the cabinet turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a drawer is a sliding part of a cabinet

explanation.surface: An award given when a government minister appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of the cabinet' suggests a government minister; it is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given in recognition, a synonym of prize.

clue.text: The Twist in the tale

parts.note: the twist in a story is read as the surname of the Dickens hero, so the first name is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: A twist in the tale is a surprise ending; capital-T Twist is the Dickens orphan.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan hero bears the surname Twist, so his forename is the 'Twist' of the novel.

clue.text: Smells nothing grim at first sniff

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing
dour means stern, grim

indicators.note: at first says take only the opening letter of sniff

explanation.surface: Unpleasant smells caught with one sniff.
explanation.definitionFit: Odours are scents or aromas, a plural synonym of smells as a noun.

clue.text: Delhi resident raised help in tavern

indicators.note: in places the reversed help word inside the tavern word

parts.note: an inn is a tavern

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the word for help is reversed

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone from Delhi lifted assistance in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is the capital of India, so someone living there is a national of that country.

clue.text: Back to fix, not front

indicators.note: not front means the first letter is dropped from the word for fix

parts.note: to mend is to fix

explanation.surface: Instructions to repair the rear rather than the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of something is its rear or back, as the back of a queue.

clue.text: Beast following most, shortly, to capital

indicators.note: following puts the beast after the shortened word
shortly means cut short, so the last letter of most is removed

parts.note: a cow is a farm beast

explanation.surface: An animal trailing behind most of the herd to a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city is the seat of government, a capital.

clue.text: Strange thing, rum, it goes to your head

parts.note: rum is old slang for odd
taken as written

indicators.note: head means the first letter of your

explanation.surface: Something peculiar: rum goes straight to your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the adjective meaning odd; 'goes to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is a peculiar thing or curiosity.

clue.text: Book-keeper scales river with Scottish man

parts.note: Libra is the zodiac sign of the scales
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An accountant climbs over a river with a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book-keeper' suggests an accountant; it means someone who keeps a library's books.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian looks after a collection of books, punningly their keeper.
